vancouver-british-columbia-kootenay-rock.title: Kootenay Rockies Weekend
vancouver-british-columbia-kootenay-rock.slogan: Two passes and 226 km, high point 950 m
vancouver-british-columbia-kootenay-rock.story: Scenery first, traffic last, with checkpoints that make sense on a bike. Out of Richmond and back again: 226 km, roughly 4 h 06 in the saddle. It goes by way of West End, Scenic stretch near Bowen Island, near Lions Bay and Maple Ridge. The climbs: Richmond and Near Maple Ridge, on the way back. It tops out at about 950 m. Much of it runs through woodland.

vancouver-british-columbia-kootenay-rock.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: Scenic stretch near Bowen Island → Photo stop near Lions Bay is the reward section in Vancouver. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.

sections.to: Near Maple Ridge, on the way back
sections.advice: Photo stop near Lions Bay → Near Maple Ridge, on the way back is shade riding: beautiful, cooler and sometimes slick. Expect damp patches, leaves, gravel and wildlife where the trees meet the road.

sections.from: Near Maple Ridge, on the way back

sections.advice: Food stop in Maple Ridge → Back to Kootenay Rockies is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.
